messages:
jordan: Received a ticket where a customer’s tool-call keeps 400ing. They pasted a curl from their terminal and we see JSON parse errors on our tool-run endpoint. Error: \"invalid character '\\n' in string literal\". attaching their curl.

ingrid: can you paste the exact payload they sent?

jordan: yep — they used a bash $'...' style literal, looks like shell expansion turned escaped sequences into actual newlines. payload:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_XXX\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  --data $'{\"tool\": \"file_search\", \"args\": {\"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\ingrid\\\\notes\\\\project\\\\readme.md\", \"query\": \"first line\\nsecond line\"}, \"sync\": true}'
```

maya: ugh, yeah — bash $'...' expands `\\n` into a literal newline in the data payload. the HTTP body the server sees contains an unescaped newline inside a JSON string, which is invalid.

alex: I reproduced locally with the exact curl. our json parser throws at the newline. sending the same body with --data-binary or using json.dumps from python works fine.

jordan: customer reported this started happening after they switched from a JS client to a quick bash snippet in their automation. they assumed $'..' is safe for json.

maya: two action items: (1) fix our support messaging to be clearer (error should hint at unescaped control characters and suggest using valid JSON quoting), (2) add a detection layer in the gateway that returns a 422 with a helpful hint if the body contains raw control chars that suggest shell-quote expansion.

alex: agree. quick repro notes for eng:
```json
{
  \"tool\": \"file_search\",
  \"args\": {
    \"path\": \"C:\\Users\\ingrid\\notes\\project\\readme.md\",
    \"query\": \"first line
second line\"
  },
  \"sync\": true
}
```
The above is invalid if the request body contains a literal CR or LF instead of the two-character escape sequence `\\n` inside the JSON string.

maya: i can add a gateway check: when Content-Type is application/json, if parsing fails and the raw body matches /\r|\n/ inside what looks like a quoted string, return 422 + header X-Redwood-Error-Hint: \"Unescaped control chars detected — ensure JSON strings use \\\\n for newlines or send as json payload from your client library\". that should cut down noise.

jordan: support response drafted: short version -> \"We see literal newlines inside a JSON string (often from bash $'...' or windows paste). Please send JSON with escaped newlines (\\n) or use --data-binary/--data-raw or an SDK call that encodes JSON. Example: curl -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" --data-binary @payload.json ...\"

ingrid: customer confirmed workaround fixed it. they changed to --data-binary and json.dumps in their python script.

support-bot: incident-note created: #INC-2026-204 — Gateway validation added to backlog. assigned to maya. ETA: next release cycle. :white_check_mark:

alex: follow-up: we'll also patch our docs (tool calling troubleshooting) with a small section: \"Common shell quoting pitfalls\" and include the curl examples.

jordan: closing ticket after patch lands and docs live. thanks everyone! :pray:
